bounded_lineage.negative_control: the independently known seed P_1 is also absent, so corpus absence is evidence about these pinned lanes only
bounded_lineage.scope: bounded nonmatch against the pinned CoxIter ordinary and index-two H10 lanes and selected local H10 ledgers; not a worldwide priority proof

K3_family.Noether_Lefschetz_argument: The nine-dimensional family therefore dominates the nine-dimensional moduli component of (11,9,1) pairs.  Extra anti-invariant algebraic classes lie on the countable union of Noether-Lefschetz hyperplanes, so the very general member has NS equal to the invariant lattice.

geometric_basis.<-2>: the nonidentity component C of the ramified I2 fiber; C^2=-2 and C is orthogonal to U and to the corrected Shioda classes
geometric_basis.E8(-2): R has no reducible fibers, so its Mordell-Weil height lattice is E8.  Pullback of its eight Shioda classes under the degree-two base change doubles every pairing, giving the orthogonal divisor lattice E8(-2).
geometric_basis.U: fiber f and O+f, where O is the zero section; their Gram is [[0,1],[1,0]]
geometric_basis.saturation: all eleven displayed divisor classes are invariant.  Their lattice has determinant 2^9, equal to the determinant forced by (r,a,delta)=(11,9,1); hence its index in H^2(X,Z)^iota is one.

nonempty_open_witness.claim_scope: this rational point proves the open is nonempty; its individual Picard lattice is not asserted to be generic

K3_family.parameter_open: Disc_t(Q) is nonzero and 4*a4^3+27*b6^2 is nonzero.  Then Q has eleven simple nonzero roots, the fiber at infinity is smooth, and all twelve singular fibers of R are I1.
K3_family.very_general_full_Picard: NS(X)=U+E8(-2)+<-2> for a very general parameter

surface_carrier.meaning: on every very-general marked member, every displayed wall is an integral divisor class and every wall reflection is an integral NS isometry
scope_exclusions: not a claim that P_N is the nef cone
not a claim that the wall classes are all irreducible curves
not a claim that the reflections are surface automorphisms

allcock_input.reference: Daniel Allcock, Infinitely many hyperbolic Coxeter groups through dimension 19, Geometry & Topology 10 (2006), 737-758
allcock_input.result_used: Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.2 (finite-subtree gluing of pairwise disjoint doubling walls)
allcock_input.walls_are_disjoint_in_H10: parallel with a common ideal point

boundary_proof.why_finite_volume: P_N is the union of N finite-volume seed chambers with pairwise disjoint interiors; Allcock proves that this union is a Coxeter polytope
boundary_proof.why_noncompact: the index-N subgroup of the nonuniform seed reflection group contains powers of its parabolic elements and is therefore still nonuniform

theorem.statement: For every integer N>=1, either N-copy finite path in the Cayley line of <s_a,s_b>=C2*C2 gives a finite-volume noncompact H10 Coxeter polytope P_N with N+12 facets. Its boundary reflections generate an index-N subgroup of the seed reflection group, and vol(P_N)=N vol(P_1). Odd N has one lattice-decorated type under path reversal; every even N has two nonisomorphic A/B types.
